title: Eagles linemen Ojomo and Johnson scuffle during final preseason practice
dek: Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Moro Ojomo and offensive tackle Fred Johnson fought during team drills on Thursday, August 13, the 11th day of training camp. The altercation started when Ojomo took exception to a late shove, escalated into punches and a tackle to the ground, and required intervention from general manager Howie Roseman, head coach Nick Sirianni, and security.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: The incident occurred on the final practice before the Eagles' preseason opener against Baltimore, with both players remaining on the field after coaches and staff separated them.
bottom_line: The incident was contained and both linemen remained on the roster heading into Saturday's preseason opener. Watch whether either player's availability changes before the Ravens game, and whether Sirianni addresses the fight in public comments on injury status or team conduct.
body: Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Moro Ojomo and offensive tackle Fred Johnson fought during team drills on Thursday, August 13, marking the 11th day of training camp. The altercation unfolded on the field's final competitive period before the Eagles' preseason opener against the Baltimore Ravens.

According to ESPN's reporting, the dust-up started when Ojomo took exception to a late shove by Johnson and squared up. Coaches decided to keep both players in for the next play. Johnson then blocked Ojomo to the ground and landed on him with his full weight, at which point punches were thrown before the two separated.

Ojomo found his way through a crowd and dove at Johnson's knees, bringing the 6-foot-7, 326-pound Johnson to the ground. Players and staff jumped in to separate the two as the altercation intensified.

General manager Howie Roseman, head coach Nick Sirianni, and chief security officer Dom DiSardo gathered around an animated Johnson to help calm him down. Roseman met with Ojomo before talking further with Johnson post-practice for about five minutes as the offensive lineman sat on blocking pads. Team drills were halted after the fight. After a group huddle to reset, the Eagles finished with a less competitive developmental period.

Before Thursday's session, Sirianni said: "I'm just so excited to see all the guys compete. At the end of the day, this business is for people that are ultracompetitive, and it's always good to go against somebody else. Sometimes at this point of camp, you're like, Man, I just want to hit somebody else and go against somebody else." The source text does not disclose whether either player sustained injury or whether any disciplinary action or fines were issued following the incident. No follow-up measures are mentioned in the reporting.
